ei.title: The Colorful Truth About Ancient Sculptures
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: In the early 1980s, Vinzenz Brinkmann was studying archaeology as a graduate student at the University of Munich. He wanted to figure out a way to closely examine the marks left by tools on ancient Greek and Roman marble sculptures, so he developed a special ultraviolet lamp that would reveal marble surfaces in great detail. When Brinkmann shone his lamp on the sculptures, he was astonished to see something that he had not expected. There were clear signs of polychromy: the use of various colors in the decoration of statues or works of architecture. Brinkmann was curious, so he decided to investigate his findings further by examining more ancient statues. To his surprise, he found evidence of polychromy on almost every statue he looked at. He soon realized that many of these traces could be detected without his special lamp. They could even be seen clearly with the naked eye. Brinkmann continued to research polychromy in ancient statues with his wife, archaeologist Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann. Their research showed undeniable evidence that, while white marble was a highly valued material for Greek and Roman sculptors, its smooth surface was not always left bare. Instead, the white marble was used like a canvas. Vivid pigments could be applied in order to decorate the sculptures in many rich colors, from yellow, red, and green to blue, pink, and even gold. Does this discovery seem surprising? If someone asks you to imagine a Greek or Roman statue, a pure white divine figure will probably come to mind. However, Brinkmann and Koch-Brinkmann’s research revealed that this image is actually inaccurate. Where did this misconception about ancient art come from, and when did it first arise? In fact, it dates back hundreds of years. White marble has been considered the standard material for sculpture in Western art since the Renaissance, when many ancient sculptures of Greece and Rome were being excavated and newly admired for their artistic beauty. Over a period of more than 1,000 years, much of the paint with which these sculptures were originally decorated wore off. Any paint that remained was faded, and more of it came off during the excavation process itself. As a result, when these ancient statues were taken out of the ground, their surfaces were plain white marble. People of the Renaissance marveled at the smoothness of the white marble and the striking manner in which it enhanced the contrast of light and shadow. In the year 1489, an ancient Roman sculpture, which became known as the Apollo Belvedere, was dug up in Italy. Renaissance artists were amazed by how its bare stone surface highlighted the elegant outline of the sculpted body. This discovery reinforced the artists’ admiration for white marble. Both artists and scholars began to associate undecorated white marble with ideal beauty. The great Renaissance artist Michelangelo was no exception. He even traveled to different quarries* around Italy in order to purchase high-quality white marble for his own sculptures. The Renaissance public’s appreciation of bare white stone led to a bias against using color to decorate sculptures, and this resulted in Renaissance artists leaving most of their marble creations unpainted. Over time, the association of whiteness with artistic beauty grew strong in people’s minds, and it became deeply rooted in Western art and culture. A German scholar who was one of the founders of art history in the West even remarked, “the whiter the body is, the more beautiful it is.” Despite the excavation of ancient Greek and Roman artifacts with traces of color in the 18th and 19th centuries, the bias toward white marble sculpture was so firmly established that people’s perceptions did not alter. Many scholars simply refused to believe that polychromy was used, while those who did were publicly criticized. Sculptures painted with bright colors and patterns were regarded as inferior works created by immature artists. Some insisted that Greek and Roman artifacts bearing obvious traces of color were in fact from other civilizations that existed before ancient Greece. Until the 1960s, sculptures with noticeable color were largely ignored. Some of them even had their colors wiped off so that the bare white surface beneath could be seen. For these reasons, the misconception that formed during the Renaissance lasted all the way into the 20th century. However, since the 1980s, thanks to the development of new methods of scientific analysis and the work of scholars such as Vinzenz Brinkmann and Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, the bias about white marble sculptures has been changing. As research has progressed, it has become increasingly clear that polychromy was not only present but also common among ancient Greek and Roman sculptures. The fact that Greek and Roman artists normally decorated their sculptures with vivid colors is now widely acknowledged. Brinkmann and Koch-Brinkmann have gathered sufficient evidence of the colorful past of many sculptures. They have also created new, colored versions of some of these great works of art, both to benefit research and to enlighten the public. These colorful recreations have been displayed in an exhibition called Gods in Color, which has traveled to over 20 different cities around the world and has expanded the understanding of millions of museum visitors since 2008. The colorful replicas are displayed next to white plaster versions made to look like the marble originals, and in some cases the originals themselves. The contrast has provided an eye-opening experience for the public, challenging artistic biases and deeply rooted misconceptions. Brinkmann believes that we need to transform our eyes into objective tools in order to overcome widespread misconceptions. There is an important lesson to be learned from this story. Shouldn’t we pause to ask ourselves if some of our long-held beliefs are the results of stereotypes and biases? Perhaps there is more to the world than meets the eye.

questions.passage: He wanted to figure out a way to closely examine the marks left by tools on ancient Greek and Roman marble sculptures, so he developed a special ultraviolet lamp that would reveal marble surfaces in great detail. When Brinkmann shone his lamp on the sculptures, he was (A)[astonished / bored] to see something that he had not expected. There were clear signs of polychromy: the use of (B)[identical / various] colors in the decoration of statues or works of architecture. Brinkmann was (C)[curious / indifferent], so he decided to investigate his findings further by examining more ancient statues. To his surprise, he found evidence of polychromy on almost every statue he looked at.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① bored(지루해하는)는 예상치 못한 것을 발견하고 '깜짝 놀란' 문맥과 반대
✅ ② astonished(깜짝 놀란)+various(다양한)+curious(호기심 있는): 예상 못 한 것을 보고 '깜짝 놀랐고', 채색(polychromy)은 '다양한' 색의 사용이며, '호기심이 생겨' 더 조사하기로 했다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ identical(똑같은)은 '다양한 색의 사용'이라는 polychromy의 정의와 반대
❌ ④ indifferent(무관심한)는 호기심이 생겨 조사를 이어 간 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: People of the Renaissance marveled at the smoothness of the white marble and the (A)[striking / dull] manner in which it enhanced the contrast of light and shadow. In the year 1489, an ancient Roman sculpture, which became known as the Apollo Belvedere, was dug up in Italy. Renaissance artists were (B)[disappointed / amazed] by how its bare stone surface highlighted the elegant outline of the sculpted body. This discovery (C)[reinforced / weakened] the artists’ admiration for white marble. Both artists and scholars began to associate undecorated white marble with ideal beauty.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① dull(흐릿한, 따분한)은 르네상스 사람들이 경탄한 '인상적인' 방식이라는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② disappointed(실망한)는 예술가들이 매끈한 표면에 '감탄했다'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ weakened(약화시켰다)는 아폴로 발견이 흰 대리석에 대한 감탄을 '강화했다'는 흐름과 반대
✅ ④ striking(인상적인)+amazed(감탄한)+reinforced(강화했다): 빛과 그림자의 대비를 돋보이게 하는 '인상적인' 방식에 경탄했고, 예술가들이 '감탄했으며', 이 발견이 흰 대리석에 대한 동경을 '강화했다'는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: Brinkmann and Koch-Brinkmann have (A)[gathered / scattered] sufficient evidence of the colorful past of many sculptures. They have also created new, colored versions of some of these great works of art, both to (B)[harm / benefit] research and to enlighten the public. These colorful recreations have been displayed in an exhibition called Gods in Color, which has traveled to over 20 different cities around the world and has (C)[expanded / narrowed] the understanding of millions of museum visitors since 2008. The colorful replicas are displayed next to white plaster versions made to look like the marble originals, and in some cases the originals themselves. The contrast has provided an eye-opening experience for the public, challenging artistic biases and deeply rooted misconceptions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① scattered(흩뜨렸다)는 증거를 충분히 '모았다'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② harm(해치다)은 연구에 '도움이 되도록' 채색 복원본을 만들었다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ③ gathered(모았다)+benefit(이롭게 하다)+expanded(넓혔다): 채색의 증거를 충분히 '모았고', 연구에 '도움이 되고' 대중을 일깨우기 위해 복원본을 만들었으며, 전시가 수백만 관람객의 이해를 '넓혔다'는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ④ narrowed(좁혔다)는 전시가 관람객의 이해를 '넓혔다'는 문맥과 반대

det.korean: ① ignore → examine: 도구가 남긴 자국을 자세히 '조사하다'(examine)
det.analysis:

✅ ④ evidence: 거의 모든 조각상에서 채색의 '증거'를 발견했다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② faded: 남아 있던 물감도 '빛이 바랬다'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ colorful(다채로운) → plain(민무늬의): 물감이 다 닳고 떨어져 나간 결과 표면이 '아무것도 없는' 흰 대리석이었다는 문맥이므로 plain이 맞다. colorful은 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ marveled: 르네상스 사람들이 매끈함에 '경탄했다'는 문맥에 적절

det.korean: ② rare → common: 채색은 존재했을 뿐 아니라 '흔했다'(common)
det.analysis:
✅ ① changing: 1980년대 이후 흰 대리석에 대한 편견이 '바뀌고 있다'는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② rare(드문) → common(흔한): 'not only present but also ~'는 '존재했을 뿐 아니라 흔하기까지 했다'는 강조 구조이므로 common이 맞다. rare는 논리적으로 모순 ← 정답
✅ ③ acknowledged: 조각상을 생생한 색으로 장식했다는 사실이 이제 널리 '인정받는다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ sufficient: 다채로웠던 과거에 대한 '충분한' 증거를 모았다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ subtle: 미미한, 알아차리기 힘든 ← 정답 (obvious의 반대)

questions.passage:
(A) A pure white marble <u>figure</u> stood at the entrance of the ancient temple. Visitors stopped to admire its elegant shape and detailed carving.
(B) The museum announced that its annual visitor <u>figure</u> had reached one million. The staff were very pleased with the number.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 figure의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) a pure white marble figure는 신전 입구에 서 있고 사람들이 형태를 감상하는 '조각상(형상)'을 뜻하고, (B) visitor figure는 백만 명에 도달했다는 '수치(숫자)'를 뜻함 ← 정답
❌ ② (A)와 (B)의 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (A)는 살아 있는 '인물'이 아니라 대리석 '조각상'
❌ ④ (B)는 '인물'이 아니라 방문객 '수치'

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"an unfair personal opinion that influences your judgment, often making you favor or oppose something without a good reason"

det.analysis:
❌ ① evidence: 증거 (어떤 것이 사실임을 보여 주는 자료)
❌ ② contrast: 대비, 대조 (둘 사이의 뚜렷한 차이)
✅ ③ bias: 편견 (타당한 이유 없이 무언가를 좋아하거나 반대하게 만드는, 판단에 영향을 주는 불공정한 개인적 견해) ← 정답
❌ ④ replica: 복제품 (원본을 똑같이 본떠 만든 것)
det.tip: bias = 판단을 치우치게 만드는 불공정한 견해, 즉 편견

questions.passage: As a result, when these ancient statues were taken out of the ground, their surfaces were plain white marble. People of the Renaissance marveled at the __________ (smooth) of the white marble and the striking manner in which it enhanced the contrast of light and shadow.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: smooth(형용사, 매끄러운) → smoothness(명사, 매끄러움): 빈칸 앞에 정관사 the가 있고 뒤에 of the white marble이 이어지므로 명사 자리다. 'marveled at the ~ of ...(~에 경탄했다)' 구조에 맞게 형용사 smooth를 명사 smoothness로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: the ___ of ~ : 관사 뒤 + of 앞 = 명사 자리 → smoothness

questions.passage: The Renaissance public’s appreciation of bare white stone led to a bias against using color to decorate sculptures, and this resulted in Renaissance artists leaving most of their marble creations unpainted. Over time, the __________ (associate) of whiteness with artistic beauty grew strong in people’s minds, and it became deeply rooted in Western art and culture.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: associate(동사, 연관 짓다) → association(명사, 연관): 빈칸 앞에 정관사 the가 있고 뒤에 of whiteness with artistic beauty가 이어지며, 빈칸이 문장의 주어(grew strong의 주체) 역할을 하므로 명사 자리다. 동사 associate를 명사 association으로 바꿔 '흰색과 예술적 아름다움의 연관'이라는 뜻을 만들어야 한다.
det.tip: the ___ of A with B가 주어 자리 → 명사 association

questions.passage: Brinkmann was curious, so he decided to investigate his findings further by examining more ancient statues.  To his surprise, he found evidence of polychromy on almost every statue he looked at.  He soon realized that many of these traces could be detected without his special lamp.  They could even be seen clearly __________.  Brinkmann continued to research polychromy in ancient statues with his wife, archaeologist Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① with the naked eye(맨눈으로): 바로 앞 문장에서 '특수 램프 없이도(without his special lamp)' 흔적을 찾을 수 있었다고 했으므로, 심지어 '맨눈으로도' 선명히 보였다는 흐름이 자연스러움 ← 정답
❌ ② under ultraviolet light(자외선 아래에서): 램프 없이도 보였다는 앞 문장과 모순
❌ ③ through special equipment(특수 장비를 통해): 특수 장비가 필요 없었다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ in the laboratory(실험실에서): 장소가 아니라 '어떻게 보이는가'가 핵심이므로 어색함
det.tip: without his special lamp → even with the naked eye: 램프 없이, 심지어 맨눈으로도

questions.passage: The colorful replicas are displayed next to white plaster versions made to look like the marble originals, and in some cases the originals themselves.  The contrast has provided an eye-opening experience for the public, challenging artistic biases and deeply rooted misconceptions.  Brinkmann believes that we need to __________ in order to overcome widespread misconceptions.  There is an important lesson to be learned from this story.  Shouldn’t we pause to ask ourselves if some of our long-held beliefs are the results of stereotypes and biases?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 transform our eyes into objective tools(우리의 눈을 객관적인 도구로 바꾸다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① preserve traditional artistic standards(전통적 예술 기준을 지키다): 편견을 '극복'하자는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② rely on our first impressions(첫인상에 의존하다): 고정관념에서 벗어나자는 글의 교훈과 반대
✅ ③ transform our eyes into objective tools(우리의 눈을 객관적인 도구로 바꾸다): 널리 퍼진 오해를 극복하기 위해 선입견 없이 '객관적으로 보아야' 한다는 Brinkmann의 주장에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ decorate sculptures with vivid colors(조각상을 생생한 색으로 장식하다): 우리가 할 일은 조각상 장식이 아니라 인식의 전환이므로 무관
det.tip: overcome widespread misconceptions → 눈을 객관적 도구로 바꿔야 한다

ch: transform our eyes into objective tools
